title: Felix and the Spire Anew
premise: Tamsin Quintana has spent twenty years guarding the Thornfell gate and pretending the old world is dead, until a child named Ilex arrives speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the Spire — the language Tamsin's own grandmother forbade in their house. The child is a living key, hunted by the court of King Aldous, whose crown was long ago fused to a memory-eating entity called the Regent that keeps him 'alive' by devouring the past of everyone who learns too much. Tamsin must smuggle Ilex through the mountains to the last dragon-fire, the only flame hot enough to unbind king from crown, while deciding whether loyalty to the family that hid them matters more than the truth they buried. In the end, Tasmisn chooses truth: the fire frees Aldous, who dies human and grateful, the Regent is starved into silence, and Tamsin reopens the gate — not as a keeper of secrets, but as a teacher of what was lost.
about_author: Beatrix Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who keep things — gates, grudge, grandmothers' silences — and what it costs to finally let go.

chapters.title: The Gate That Stays Shut
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A quiet winter night at the Thornfell gate establishes Tamsin's routines, their grandmother's rules, and the smugglers' roads only they know. When a knock comes at midnight, Tamsin opens the door on instinct — and finds a child speaking words that make the stones hum. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the past knocking literally.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin recognizes fragments of the child's speech from half-buried childhood memories and realizes Ilex speaks the Spire-tongue their grandmother burned books to erase. Ilex carries a dragon-scale token and says one clear word: 'Spire.' Emotional beat: dread and reluctant wonder as Tamsin's carefully buried inheritance resurfaces.

chapters.title: Riders on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV, rendered in close third. Royal riders reach the valley asking after a runaway, offering silver for silence. Tamsin lies smoothly, but Ilex sees how the captain's shadow moves wrong — the Regent's mark. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the child understands the hunters better than the keeper does.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching the cellar, Tamsin finds their grandmother's hidden ledger: the Quintana family were Spire-keepers for generations, and the gate doesn't lock something out — it locks something down. The first entry names the Regent. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into grief; loyalty to the dead woman warring with her lies.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dual focus, mostly Tamsin's POV. Tamsin calls in an old debt with Ferro, a smuggler with a mule train and no questions, to move Ilex over the pass before the thaw closes the high roads. Ferro extracts a price: the truth about what they're carrying. Emotional beat: wary alliance; trust extended as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Crown of Hungry Years
chapters.summary: King Aldous's POV — brief, fragmented, memory-slipping. In the capital, we see the king inside his own head, watching the Regent wear him, hoarding stolen memories like coins. He senses the dragon-scale moving toward the mountains. Emotional beat: tragic claustrophobia; the antagonist is also a prisoner.

chapters.title: The Pass of Ashen Bells
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ambushed on the high pass by Regent-bound soldiers, the party scatters; Ferro takes a wound covering Ilex's escape, and Tamsin kills for the first time in twenty years of keeping peace. Emotional beat: shattering of the invisible life; guilt braided with fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They reach the drowned forge beneath the Spire where the final dragon-fire gutters in its stone cradle, fed by nothing but old vows. To feed it, someone must give it a true memory — willingly, permanently. Emotional beat: awe and sacrifice; the theme made literal.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin and Aldous POVs. Tamsin feeds the fire their dearest memory — their grandmother's voice singing — and the flame roars up the mountain to the crown. Aldous, given one lucid hour, chooses to stand still and let the fire take the Regent and himself together. Emotional beat: climax; grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: The Gate, Opened
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV, closing. Spring comes. With the Regent starved and the king mourned honestly rather than mythologized, Tamsin unlocks the Thornfell gate and begins teaching the Spire-tongue to anyone who wants it — starting with Ilex. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance reclaimed as gift instead of burden.
